Hey guys. This isn't the usual kind of discussion I see on this subverse, but it's something I've had on my mind, and I want to see if anyone has any thoughts.

I've noticed a lot of people from outside the reddit community commenting on the events of the past few weeks, and they seem to view the ordeal as somewhat of am example of the state of communities on the internet, rather than just a piece of the online group we all knew so well. What I'm wondering is, do you think a large part of this community leaving so abruptly says more about the way people connect online to begin with it, or is it more of a drama that unfolded by itself?

I hope I'm phrasing this decently, and I know it's sort of a weird question, but I was curious to see if this had occurred to anybody.
Did the drama and/or subsequent mass exodus from reddit have more to do with reddit itself, or with online communities as a whole?
I'd say it represents online communites as a whole. It boils down to human nature and I think there are too many racists, sexists, homophobes, etc. in the world to be civil online.

I think most online communities are fickle, especially when they get big ... there's very little real 'connection' to the site. We saw it with Digg, we're now seeing it with Reddit. There's also a herd mentality, if enough content creators leave then the audience will follow.
I'm not sure I understand what you mean by "online communities". Can you explain?

With you on that one. You couldn't mutter a sentence without someone being "triggered".

I'd say it's a broader thing.

A similar exodus from 4chan to 8chan happened last year.

Conscientious users got fed up with progressive, interventionist moderation and left. The teeming masses didn't care and stayed.

Seems to be going around lately.

I think a lot of people are in shock and awe about what happened.

Most communities of humans have forces that keep people from leaving when things get shitty. Money, borders and laws stifle human movement. As a result, leaders have developed a habit of passing down shitty rules that the captive population have no choice but to deal with. Online communities don't have the restrictions of a physical population. People can go where they want. If the grass is greener on another site, there are no passports or immigration to make them stay put. Admins ignored this simple principle. I've seen it happen before. I remember when Yahoo overestimated the attraction of their news network and destroyed geocities. Yahoo still hasn't recovered from that exodus. MySpace also never recovered. You have leadership trying to treat users as if they are a stationary irl population with limited choices and it blows up in their faces every time. CEOs, admins, board members all failed to realize that the users control the site. Always have and there is nothing they can do to change that without alienating the very users they depend on.
